purpose: Pre-edit isolated baseline required by Fresh rebuild comparison step 1 and step 4, so every regression reference in the Gates section has a paired same-machine pre-change sample. Captured before the first edit to graph_indexer.py, graph_cluster.py or the state-store schema.

baseline.working_tree_note: The snapshot is of the working tree at that HEAD, not of the commit. The source fingerprint below, not the sha, is the authority for what was built.

source_snapshot.fingerprint_basis: sha256 over the canonical JSON of {repo-relative path: sha256 of file bytes} for every eligible file

driver.provenance: Own driver. The 1xny3 drivers (docs/waves/1xny3 sqlite-graph-consolidation-evaluation/graph_lifecycle_eval.py commands rebuild/deltas/reset-deltas and graph_eval.py) stage under the repository root and read .wavefoundry/index; this capture may do neither. Their approach was reused: freeze an eligible cohort, drive the ACTUAL producer in an isolated root, time source-change-to-artifact, and assert a from-scratch oracle against the incremental result. The delta fixture (lifecycle_fixture caller/provider/guide and the bound/renamed/removed cycle) is theirs verbatim.

builder_version_bump_rebuild.scope: builder-version-bump rebuild: a completed graph state whose stored meta.builder_version was rewritten in the SCRATCH store only, so GraphStateStore.ensure_current() resets it and the session re-extracts every file. No framework source was edited.
builder_version_bump_rebuild.how_the_bump_was_forced: After a completed rebuild the SCRATCH store stage/.wavefoundry/index/graph/project-graph-state.sqlite had its meta.builder_version row rewritten from 51 to 50 with plain SQL. That is exactly the value GraphStateStore.ensure_current() compares, so the next session called reset() and the whole corpus was re-extracted. No framework source was edited and the repository store was not touched.
builder_version_bump_rebuild.community_caveat: The forced bump changes only the stored version, so the emitted graph and its input_fingerprint are unchanged and update_graph_clusters reused the existing cluster artifact (0.024 s) instead of recomputing. A real builder bump that changes emitted graph content also pays the community recompute, which the fresh rebuilds above measure at about 4.485 s. Compare the extraction phase, not the total, when pairing this case.
builder_version_bump_rebuild.regression_reference: pair against the graph_extract_resolve_persist_s value of 159.972 s

legacy_schema_fixture.capture_method: The producer tree at each commit was materialized with git archive and run against a fresh temporary store through a recording connection wrapper; the executed CREATE statements on the store's own connection were kept, including the DDL schema 7 delegates to sqlite_vector_store.create_schema. Replaying each list on a bare stdlib sqlite3 database reproduces the producer's sqlite_schema objects exactly.

graph_parity_fixture.repeatability: three independent builds produced identical normalized output

qualification.purpose: Fresh rebuild comparison steps 2-4 and AC-9's production-path measurements, paired against the pre-change baseline this file already carries. Built from the SAME frozen source snapshot L1 froze, on the same machine, interpreter and backends.

schema_8_dispatch_precondition.rule: AC-9: every recorded timing is preconditioned on meta.store_schema_version == 8 on the MEASURED store, so a no-op upgrade cannot yield vacuous numbers.

driver.pairing_method: L1's driver is imported and its PURE normalization helpers (canon, sha_value, stable_payload, stable_communities, edge_multiset, coverage, summarize) are reused by reference, so the two sides cannot drift in how a digest is computed. Only the store-shaped parts are re-implemented.
driver.production_shape: The COORDINATED path: graph prepare -> cluster prepare -> publication.community = cluster_publication -> one BEGIN IMMEDIATE .. COMMIT, mirroring indexer._build_graph_artifacts and the coordinator's publication transaction. Production never calls these producers without state_conn; the standalone branch would write the cluster artifact as JSON into the retired graph folder and publish no community rows, so measuring it would not measure the shipped path.
driver.instrumentation: Observation only. sqlite_runtime.connect is wrapped so every returned apsw connection carries an exec tracer and a statement profile. No product statement, order or transaction boundary is altered. The tracer fires AFTER a statement completes, so the recorded window is 'after BEGIN IMMEDIATE returns' to 'after COMMIT returns' -- the interval the write lock is actually HELD. Lock WAIT is reported separately from the BEGIN IMMEDIATE statement profile and is not counted in the held segment.
driver.isolation: Every build ran under /private/tmp/1xny6-r2/qualify/. The repository working tree and .wavefoundry/index/ were never written.

normalizations_applied_and_why.reason: per-run merge counters and timings, never persisted

filesystem locator for the RETIRED derived cluster artifact; the consolidated store writes no cluster JSON. This is the only normalization beyond L1's own volatile-bookkeeping set, it is applied to the BASELINE side, and with it applied the two community digests are byte-identical.

graph_content_parity.nothing_normalized_away: No node, edge, evidence string, confidence value, multiplicity, community id or membership list was normalized on either side.

dimensions.basis: nodes sorted by id; every node field retained (id, label, kind, source_file, source_location, layer, external and all extractor attributes)

every edge collapsed into a multiset keyed on the canonical JSON of the WHOLE edge record (source, target, relation, confidence, evidence, self_edge_kind and attributes) with an explicit multiplicity, so a lost or gained duplicate is visible
files in merge, files with extracted nodes, per-source-file node census digest, edges per relation and edges per confidence

the_only_difference.why_this_is_bookkeeping_not_content: cluster_path is a FILESYSTEM LOCATOR for the retired derived cluster artifact, not graph or community content. The consolidated store publishes community rows and writes no cluster JSON, so the key has nothing to point at. Removing this one key from the baseline payload makes the two digests byte-identical: every community id, label, seed node, node count, membership list, betweenness value and projection rule is unchanged. No membership, no identity and no confidence value was normalized.
the_only_difference.diff_method: whole-payload key-by-key diff of the two archived community payloads: keys only in baseline = ['cluster_path'], keys only in new store = [], changed keys shared by both = []

documented_nondeterminism_accounted_for.community_detection: leiden via igraph+leidenalg on both sides. graph_cluster seeds igraph's global RNG and passes leidenalg seed=0 before partitioning; community ordering is a fixed (-size, seed_node_id) sort. The measured outcome is stronger than 'accounted for': all four independent new-store builds produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL community payload, and it equals the baseline's. No difference was attributed to nondeterminism, because none was observed.
documented_nondeterminism_accounted_for.graph_parallel_backend: threads on both sides (WAVEFOUNDRY_GRAPH_PARALLEL_BACKEND default). Parallel code extraction could in principle reorder merge inputs; the identical node, edge-multiset and coverage digests across four builds show it did not.

independent_expected_result_fixtures.why: Agreement between the two graph paths cannot by itself prove correctness -- both could share a defect. These expectations were authored against NEITHER build.

B_coordinated_production_shape.the_only_difference: the same retired cluster_path locator; community ids and membership are identical (membership_identical=true)
B_coordinated_production_shape.communities_read_back_from_rows_equal_pr: the prepared payload carries a 'present' boolean that graph_cluster.read_published_clusters does not reconstruct; no community id, membership, count or betweenness value differs

cache_reuse_not_per_query_hydration.verdict: Cache reuse is demonstrated on both sides: the second call returns the SAME object and costs a small fraction of the first. The new store's warm re-entry costs 5.1 ms against 0.13 ms because get_query_index now takes a graph_snapshot generation pin on every call (the AC-5 coherence contract) where the pre-change path did one filesystem stat. That is a per-call PIN, not a per-call hydration: hydration is 656 ms and happens once.

ac9_measurements.reporting_rule: Every number below is a measurement, not a target. Where a value misses its screen it is reported as a miss with the number. No measurement was tuned to meet a screen.

public_query_latency_and_parity.protocol: Gates readiness comparison protocol: warm resident cache, 10 warm-ups and 100 measured observations per family per run, three runs, pooled p50/p95/p99. One observation is ONE public call, so a p95 is directly comparable to a Gates screen. No family was truncated by the time budget.
public_query_latency_and_parity.parity: every one of the nine families returned byte-identical results

one_family_slower.what_it_is: server_impl._graph_references_candidate_files -- the graph-derived candidate-file restriction the public code_references path applies BEFORE any ranking. Ranking settings were not touched by this lane.
one_family_slower.mechanism: Not per-call hydration. get_query_index now wraps the whole call in a graph_snapshot.pinned(root, layer) generation pin -- the AC-5 coherence contract -- where the pre-change path did one filesystem stat of the payload file. The constructed index is still cached and reused (same object returned). The cost is the per-call PIN: corroborated independently by the warm second get_query_index call, 5.1 ms new versus 0.13 ms pre-change.
one_family_slower.disposition: Reported, not adjudicated. 4.0 ms p50 / 4.6 ms p95 absolute, no Gates screen applies, and it buys the generation coherence AC-5 requires. Flagged for the implementation lane to accept or reduce.

startup.verdict: REPORTED, no screen. Cold hydration is 2.18x slower on the shared store (656 ms against 300 ms) and costs 38 percent LESS resident memory (219 MB against 354 MB). Both are real and neither is screened.

process_resident_memory.method: ps -o rss sampled from a background thread in the measuring process

query_serving_after_hydration_bytes.reading: the shared store serves the same graph with ~135 MB less resident memory

overlapping_generations_scenario.what_it_does: hydrates the OLD generation, starts a thread running wf_graph_report's engine (GraphQueryIndex.report) continuously, then publishes an incremental generation and hydrates the NEW one while the report thread is still in flight, so both resident generations overlap
overlapping_generations_scenario.reading: Two resident graph generations plus an in-flight report cost about 35 MB more than one, and the old generation's memory is returned when it is released. 7,556 reports completed across the publication with zero errors, so a reader in flight is not disturbed by the commit.

inclusive_published_cost.note: graph-only content; this store carries no semantic vectors, so it is not comparable to the 266.8 MiB authoritative-disk figure in the Gates section, which includes semantic data.

wal_frames_written_per_incremental_publi.how_it_was_measured: The WAL is auto-checkpointed and removed when the last connection closes, so sampling after a publication reads 0 and tells you nothing. The figure above is taken from the held-reader scenario, where a reader pins a snapshot across the publication and therefore PREVENTS the checkpoint, leaving the frames the publication actually wrote observable.
wal_frames_written_per_incremental_publi.at_rest_explanation: 0 is the correct at-rest value and is not a measurement failure: the publication's frames are checkpointed back into the main database and the WAL is removed on close.

memory_map_window_against_file_size.reading: the retained 256 MiB window still covers this 173.4 MiB store with about 82.6 MiB of headroom; a store past 256 MiB would fall back to ordinary reads beyond the window rather than fail

staging_and_rollback_peak.why_not: Measuring the upgrade's staging peak end to end requires a REAL schema-7 index-state.sqlite with semantic content and a receipt produced by prepare_upgrade, then migrate_legacy driven under an upgrade context. L1's frozen baseline contains no semantic index (it is a graph-only capture), so no such source exists in this lane's isolated tree, and a synthetic near-empty schema-7 store would produce a disk figure with no meaning. Stated as not measured rather than estimated.
staging_and_rollback_peak.what_is_known_structurally_without_measu: Procedure step 3 stages beside the owned index and step 4 retains rollback identities until fresh-process verification finishes, so peak inclusive disk during a conversion is bounded below by source plus staged candidate. No numeric claim is made here.

held_reader_scenario.what_it_asserts: a reader pins a snapshot through one incremental publication, then releases; the WAL must fall below its auto-checkpoint threshold within the NEXT publication
held_reader_scenario.reading: The pinned reader saw a stable 46,668-node snapshot straight through the commit. Its pin held the WAL at 8,272 bytes -- 0.2 percent of the 4,120,000 byte auto-checkpoint threshold -- and the next publication after release returned it to 0. Long-lived-reader checkpoint pressure is not a problem at this change size.

import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
sys.path.insert(0, '/private/tmp/1xny6-r2/qualify')
import qualify_new as q

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory)/'probe.sqlite'
    blocker = q._orig_connect(path)
    blocker.execute('CREATE TABLE probe(value)')
    blocker.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
    waiting = threading.Event()
    result = {}
    class DelayedCommit:
        def __init__(self, conn): self.conn = conn
        def execute(self, sql, *a, **kw):
            if sql == 'COMMIT': time.sleep(.1)
            return self.conn.execute(sql, *a, **kw)
        def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(self.conn, name)
    def writer():
        native = q._orig_connect(path)
        conn = q._ObservedConnection(DelayedCommit(native), path)
        waiting.set()
        conn.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
        conn.execute('INSERT INTO probe VALUES(1)')
        conn.execute('COMMIT')
        native.close()
    q.tx_reset()
    thread = threading.Thread(target=writer)
    thread.start()
    assert waiting.wait(5)
    time.sleep(.3)
    blocker.execute('COMMIT')
    blocker.close()
    thread.join(5)
    assert not thread.is_alive()
    result = q.tx_summary()
    assert result['begin_immediate_statement_ms'][0] >= 250, result
    assert 90 <= result['lock_held_ms'][0] < 250, result
    print(json.dumps(result))

"""Real all-content coordinator qualification; private scratch roots only."""
import argparse
import contextlib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import resource
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('--scripts', required=True)
p.add_argument('--root', required=True)
p.add_argument('--out', required=True)
p.add_argument('--sources', required=True)
p.add_argument('--label', required=True)
p.add_argument('--seed-index')
p.add_argument('--skip-full', action='store_true')
args = p.parse_args()
root = Path(args.root).resolve()
assert str(root).startswith('/private/tmp/1xny6-repair-perf/')
sys.path.insert(0, args.scripts)
import indexer
import index_state_store as iss
import sqlite_runtime as runtime
import sqlite_vector_store as vectors

if root.exists():
    raise RuntimeError('Use a fresh scratch root')
shutil.copytree(args.sources, root, symlinks=True)
index_dir = root / '.wavefoundry/index'
assert not index_dir.exists()
if args.seed_index:
    index_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(args.seed_index, index_dir / iss.STATE_STORE_FILENAME)
    seed_store = iss.IndexStateStore(index_dir, migration=True)
    seed_store.close()


spans = []
phases = []
real_connect = runtime.connect

class Connection:
    def __init__(self, conn, path):
        self.conn, self.path, self.span = conn, str(path), None
    def execute(self, sql, *a, **kw):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = self.conn.execute(sql, *a, **kw)
        returned = time.perf_counter()
        head = sql.strip().upper()
        if head == 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE':
            self.span = {'path': self.path, 'begin_returned': returned,
                         'acquisition_ms': (returned-start)*1000}
            spans.append(self.span)
        elif head in ('COMMIT', 'ROLLBACK') and self.span is not None:
            self.span.update(end_returned=returned, outcome=head,
                             held_ms=(returned-self.span['begin_returned'])*1000)
            self.span = None
        return result
    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self.conn, name)
    def __enter__(self):
        self.conn.__enter__()
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *a):
        return self.conn.__exit__(*a)

runtime.connect = lambda path, **kw: Connection(real_connect(path, **kw), path)
real_apply = vectors.PreparedUpdates.apply
def apply(self, store, **kw):
    phases.append({'phase': 'semantic_apply', 'at': time.perf_counter()})
    return real_apply(self, store, **kw)
vectors.PreparedUpdates.apply = apply
gi = indexer._get_graph_indexer()
if hasattr(gi, 'GraphPublication'):
    real_graph = gi.GraphPublication.apply
    def graph(self, conn):
        phases.append({'phase': 'graph_apply', 'at': time.perf_counter()})
        return real_graph(self, conn)
    gi.GraphPublication.apply = graph

def disk():
    paths = list(index_dir.rglob('*')) if index_dir.exists() else []
    files = [(f, f.stat().st_size) for f in paths if f.is_file()]
    return {'total_bytes': sum(n for _,n in files),
            'prepared_bytes': sum(n for f,n in files if 'wavefoundry-sqlite-prepared-' in str(f)),
            'wal_bytes': sum(n for f,n in files if f.name.endswith('-wal'))}

records = []
def run(label, full=False):
    spans.clear(); phases.clear()
    samples = []; stopped = threading.Event()
    def sample():
        while not stopped.is_set():
            try:
                rss = int(subprocess.check_output(['ps','-o','rss=','-p',str(os.getpid())]))*1024
                samples.append({'rss_bytes': rss, **disk()})
            except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
                pass
            stopped.wait(.25)
    sampler = threading.Thread(target=sample)
    sampler.start()
    log = io.StringIO()
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(log), contextlib.redirect_stderr(log):
            result = indexer.build_index(root, full=full, verbose=False, content='all')
    finally:
        wall = time.perf_counter()-start
        stopped.set(); sampler.join()
        Path(args.out+'.'+label+'.log').write_text(log.getvalue())
    if result.get('error') or result.get('failed'):
        raise RuntimeError(result)
    state = iss.read_build_state(index_dir)
    assert state['status'] == 'complete', state
    conn = iss.open_read_only(index_dir)
    try:
        schema = conn.execute("SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='store_schema_version'").fetchone()[0]
        counts = {l: conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM chunks_'+l).fetchone()[0] for l in ('docs','code')}
        assert all(counts.values()), counts
        pragma = {k: conn.execute('PRAGMA '+k).fetchone()[0] for k in ('page_size','mmap_size','wal_autocheckpoint','freelist_count')}
        layers = list(conn.execute('SELECT * FROM build_layer_state')) if schema == '8' else None
    finally:
        conn.close()
    anchors = [x['at'] for x in phases if x['phase']=='semantic_apply']
    publications = [s for s in spans if any(s['begin_returned'] <= a <= s.get('end_returned',0) for a in anchors)]
    assert publications and all(s['outcome']=='COMMIT' for s in publications), (spans,phases)
    if schema == '8':
        assert any(x['phase']=='graph_apply' for x in phases), phases
    rec = {'label':label,'wall_s':wall,'publication':publications,'phases':[dict(x) for x in phases],'schema':schema,
           'counts':counts,'state':state,'layers':layers,'pragma':pragma,'disk_after':disk(),
           'peak':{k:max(s[k] for s in samples) for k in samples[0]} if samples else {},
           'samples':len(samples),'sample_interval_s':.25,'process_peak_rss_bytes':resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss}
    records.append(rec)
    Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps({'label':args.label,'scripts':args.scripts,
        'source_manifest':str(Path(args.sources).parent/'source-manifest.json'),
        'records':records,'runtime':{'python':sys.version,'apsw':runtime.apsw.apswversion(),
                                    'sqlite':runtime.apsw.sqlitelibversion()},
        'limitations':'Native macOS ARM64 only; real local embedder; sampled RSS/disk can miss sub-250ms peaks.'},indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps({'label':label,'wall_s':wall,'held_ms':[s['held_ms'] for s in publications],
                      'counts':counts,'peak':rec['peak']}),flush=True)

run('seed_update' if args.skip_full else 'full', full=not args.skip_full)
probe = root/'lifecycle_fixture/coordinator_probe.py'
probe.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
for n in range(10):
    probe.write_text(f'def coordinator_probe_{n}(value):\n    return value + {n}\n')
    run('delta-'+str(n))
